svg.text: Transactional outbox: how an event gets from one bounded context to another
Problem: saving to the database and sending to Kafka cannot happen in one step. If one fails, data and events disagree.
Solution: save the event in the same database transaction as the change, and let a separate Outbox-Service send it.
Provided library, used inside your service
Other boxes: provided infrastructure (Outbox-Service, Kafka, PostgreSQL)

g.text: same key → same partition → in order
calls the right handler for each event type
b. older than what I have? → skip (late)

svg.text: Never send to Kafka from your service. Write events to the outbox in the same transaction (4).
Every message can arrive twice. A crash between 6 and 7 sends it again: handle duplicates (a).
Order holds per aggregate only. Same key, same partition. Late messages are skipped (b).
C4 Level 2: the Outbox-Service is a container; the libraries are code inside containers (no boxes).
At least once: nothing is lost, but duplicates are possible.
ECST: event-carried state transfer, the full state as a message.
Revision: 1, 2, 3 … per aggregate; tells old from new.
DLT: dead-letter topic, where failing messages are parked.
Usually: listen to the events OR the state, one listener each.
